message:
Make era_2026_1.html the main game version

Replace the game file with the version the user supplied
(era_2026_1.html), byte for byte, with nothing added. Every earlier
version, including all features built in this branch, stays in the git
history so any of them can be brought back on request.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Map: back to the previous tiles

Restore the Esri satellite view with its Boundaries and Places overlay,
and the original Dark political, Light atlas and Terrain maps, as
requested. The CARTO labels layer (which now requires an API key and
stamped "API KEY REQUIRED" on the map) and the tinted physical-map
bases are removed. The 14-day cooldown and drawing highlighted
countries above their neighbours stay.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

14-day cooldown after every answer; one set of borders, highlights on top

Cooldown:
- A country now waits 14 days after any answer, yes or no, before it
  looks at another proposal of the same kind from you (written
  agreements and every treaty in the Propose list). The bar says
  whether it signed or turned down the last one, and sits under the
  country picker so it shows even after a signed draft is cleared.

Borders:
- The map tiles no longer draw borders of their own. The satellite
  view used Esri's "Boundaries and Places" overlay, whose borders did
  not match the game's (and knew nothing of the new states), giving
  doubled, offset lines. It now uses a labels-only layer (CARTO, place
  names only); Terrain does the same, and Dark political / Light atlas
  use a border-free physical relief map, tinted dark or light, under
  the same labels. Every border on screen is now the game's own.
- A highlighted country (yours, the selected one, or the one under the
  mouse) is drawn above its neighbours, so its whole outline shows
  instead of being half-covered by the next country's border; after
  hovering, your country and the selected one go back on top. Round
  line joins, full opacity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Agreement drafts: never rejected, made workable, and laid out like a real treaty

Never rejected:
- "Write the draft" no longer refuses an idea. Your staff keep the main
  idea and change only what could not be signed: demands for a whole
  territory, treasury, army or resources become proportionate terms,
  "become our colony" becomes close foreign-policy coordination,
  "for free" becomes preferential prices, impossible percentages are
  capped, clauses disposing of a third country's territory are left
  out, a list of demands gets an offer in return, and a one-word idea
  becomes a cooperation framework. Each change is listed above the
  draft. The AI is told the same: never refuse, make it feasible,
  keep the main idea, and list what it changed.
- Better reading of plain ideas: "gives/becomes/hands over" verbs,
  "X and us agree that ...", "they give us X in return for Y",
  "for free", country adjectives in any case (and misspelt ones).

Realistic document:
- Formal state names (the Russian Federation, the Republic of
  Belarus ...) in the title, preamble and signature blocks, a proper
  preamble ("Desiring ... Guided by ... Have agreed as follows"),
  centred article numbers and headings, and a "Done at <capital> on
  <date>, in two originals, each in the <languages> ..." clause.
- Your country's national emblem (coat of arms, from Wikipedia; the
  flag when offline) heads the page, and a round red ink seal of your
  Ministry of Foreign Affairs with the emblem in the middle is stamped
  beside your signature. The other side's block waits for signature.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Treaty cooldown: 14 days after a refusal, shown as a progress bar

- After a government turns down a written agreement or a treaty from
  the Propose list, it waits 14 days (was 20 / 30) before looking at
  the same kind of proposal from you again. A signed deal no longer
  starts a cooldown, so close partners can sign one agreement after
  another.
- Instead of the "wants more time" message, a progress bar shows how
  far through the 14 days you are ("day 5 of 14 · 9 days left") under
  the draft or the Propose row, and the Send / Propose button stays
  disabled until it runs out.
- The Propose row remembers the chosen country and treaty type, and
  old result messages are cleared when you pick another country or
  write a new draft, so a stale message no longer lingers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Fix allies refusing agreements: the "already allied" penalty only blocks a second defence pact

treatyScore took 100 points off whenever the two countries already
shared a defence pact or alliance, whatever was being proposed. That
was meant to stop a duplicate mutual-defence pact, but it made real
allies (Russia-Belarus via the CSTO, USA-UK, France-Germany, USA-Japan
...) refuse even simple investment, energy or trade deals. Now the
penalty only applies to defence pacts and alliances; for every other
treaty an existing alliance adds +20 and is named as a reason.

For written agreements the connected AI is told the real relationship
(relations label and the treaties already binding the two countries),
a very close partner no longer refuses a reasonable deal just because
the AI said no, and a refusal letter is never shown on a signed deal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Agreements fill their own gaps; realistic 1 January 2026 relations

Agreements:
- When a draft is written, your staff estimate how far the partner is
  from signing and add balancing clauses, most relevant first, until it
  should pass: not directed against third States (if the partner's
  allies dislike you), respect for sovereignty (cool relations),
  concessional development financing scaled to the partner (more
  persuasive for poorer countries), market access, technical
  assistance, a review clause. Added articles are marked in the draft,
  an outlook line says whether the partner is likely to sign and what
  the clauses will cost, and the costs are paid on signing. When no
  clause could close the gap, nothing is given away.
- The connected AI is told to keep those clauses when it rewrites.
- Civil agreements no longer take a 25-point hit for every ally of the
  partner that dislikes you (that rule is for defence pacts); it now
  counts once, more for security and intelligence deals.

Relations:
- Pairs without a recorded relationship are no longer a flat 0: they
  now follow camp alignment (Western vs Russia/China/Iran), regional
  families (African Union, Arab League, Latin America, Caribbean, SCO,
  Nordic, Anglosphere, Turkic states, Pacific, Central Asia),
  neighbourhood and shared faith.
- About 300 more specific relationships as of 1 January 2026 (US
  tariff partners, Russia's neighbours, Gulf, South and East Asia,
  Africa, Latin America, and the non-state actors with their patrons
  and hosts).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Agreements: custom duration in months or years, and agreements expire

- The Duration menu (5/10/15/25 years) is replaced by a number box and a
  months/years choice (1-1200 months or 1-100 years). A length written
  in the idea itself ("for 18 months", "for 3 years") fills it in.
- The draft's duration article uses that exact term, with a notice
  period that fits it (seven days, one month or six months), and the
  AI is given the same term.
- Signed written agreements now expire when their term ends: "Your
  treaties" shows the time left, and on expiry the agreement is marked
  expired, the feed says so and the partner writes that it is open to
  a new one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Agreements: one simple idea in, instant formal draft out

- One box for your idea in plain words (e.g. "cheap oil for them in
  exchange for lower tariffs on our goods"), plus six clickable example
  ideas; Enter writes the draft. The offer/ask boxes are gone.
- The legal staff work out who does what from the sentence (we / they /
  both, "X for Y", "in return for", lists joined by commas or "and")
  and produce the formal draft instantly (~10 ms) instead of waiting
  for the AI.
- With an AI engine connected, it then expands the same idea in the
  background (shorter prompt, 900-token budget) into full treaty
  language and swaps it in when ready; the staff draft can be sent
  meanwhile. If the AI finds the idea doesn't make sense, it says why.
- Same checks as before: you must give something, nothing absurd,
  nothing binding third countries. A duration in the idea ("for 15
  years") overrides the Duration menu.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Agreements: set the main ideas, get a formal draft to send or clear

The write-your-own-agreement box is replaced by an idea-based drafter:
choose the country and a duration, list what you offer and what you ask
in return (one idea per line, or click from 10 suggested ideas on each
side), and press "Write the draft". The ideas are checked first (you
must offer something; nothing absurd; nothing binding third countries).

With an AI engine connected, it writes a formal treaty (title, preamble,
5-8 articles including each side's undertakings, implementation,
duration, dispute settlement and entry into force) or explains why the
ideas don't work. Without one, the legal staff build the same structure
from standard treaty templates, turning ideas into "X shall ..." clauses
written from your side. The draft is shown as a document with
signature lines and "Send to <country>" / "Clear" (or "Rewrite the
draft"). Signed agreements keep their full text, folded under "Read
the text" in Your treaties.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Treaties: energy, technology and intelligence agreements + write-your-own agreements

- New treaty types in the Treaties menu, with real effects on signing:
  energy partnership (growth for both, more when the partner is a big
  energy exporter), technology-sharing agreement (your growth, more
  with a stronger partner; partner's rivals -3) and intelligence-
  sharing agreement (+2 stability; partner's rivals -5). Accepted AI
  offers now apply treaty effects too, and leaving a non-military pact
  costs less credibility.
- "Write your own agreement": pick any government, write the terms,
  and "Check the draft" first. It must make sense as an agreement
  between the two governments: long enough, with concrete commitments,
  proportionate terms, no clauses binding third countries, not only
  demands on the other side. With an AI engine connected, the other
  government's treaty office reads it (and later decides as that
  government); without one the offline staff check it with rules. A
  valid draft is shown as a title, type and clean clauses before you
  propose it. Signed agreements list their clauses under Your treaties
  and give effects by type (trade, energy, technology, security...).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Theocracies of any religion, no emojis in Politics, "Non-state actors" tab

- Politics tab: emojis removed from the system cards, buttons and the
  related feed messages.
- Theocracy now has a State religion picker (Sunni Islam, Shia Islam,
  Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant Christianity, Judaism, Hinduism,
  Buddhism, Sikhism). Countries now carry a majority faith; the chosen
  faith sets relations (same-faith countries +10, same-faith
  theocracies +15, other theocracies -10) and approval (-8 for the
  people's own faith, -25 otherwise). A theocracy can change its state
  religion later. The system is shown as e.g. "Theocracy (Shia Islam)";
  Iran is Shia, Afghanistan Sunni and the Vatican a Catholic theocracy.
- "Proxies & militias" is renamed "Non-state actors" (tab, idea list,
  help text, map-layer toggle), and its intro now says the groups
  appear on the map as states of their own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Add the Suwayda Druze authority (Israel-backed) and a political-system changer

- Suwayda (Druze): a new state carved out of Syria from the real
  As-Suwayda governorate outline, minus the western villages held by
  government forces and tribes since July 2025 and the empty eastern
  desert. Led by Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri (Supreme Legal Committee,
  National Guard), backed by Israel, hostile to Damascus; "Druze",
  "Sweida", "Jabal Bashan" etc. resolve to it in orders.
- Government > Politics now has "Change your political system": all
  seven systems with what each changes (elections, coup risk,
  relations, approval). Switch by constitutional reform (90-180 days,
  40 political capital in democracies, passes only with approval of
  at least 35%) or by decree (immediate, bigger approval and relations
  hit). The new system takes effect everywhere: elections, political
  capital, coup risk and relations with like-minded countries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Aligned borders, regions & provinces, Hezbollah heartlands + political wing

- Borders: simplification is now topology-preserving. Every border is
  split where its neighbours change and each stretch is simplified once,
  in a fixed direction, so both sides (and the selection highlight) use
  exactly the same line: no gaps, overlaps or offset outlines between
  countries or the carved-out states.
- Regions & provinces: Natural Earth admin-1 (4,486 subdivisions, public
  domain) is embedded in a compact form. Internal province borders are
  drawn as faint dashed lines once you zoom in (on their own
  non-interactive pane), hovering shows "Country · Province · Region",
  and the country panel lists its regions and provinces and names the
  one you clicked.
- Hezbollah's state now covers its heartlands: the south up to the
  Zahrani/Nabatieh and the western Bekaa, the Baalbek–Hermel Bekaa, and
  Dahiyeh. Lebanon's own panel shows Hezbollah's political wing
  (Loyalty to the Resistance bloc, Shia duo with Amal) alongside the
  state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Taliban flag for Afghanistan; South Lebanon as shared Lebanese/Hezbollah influence

- Afghanistan now shows the Taliban (Islamic Emirate) flag: white field
  with the black shahada, drawn inline so it works everywhere flags show.
- The Hezbollah area is now "South Lebanon" under the Lebanese flag and
  Lebanon's political system. Selecting it shows a Shared influence
  section: Lebanese government (Joseph Aoun, Nawaf Salam) 45% and
  Hezbollah (Naim Qassem) 55%, with the leader card reading
  "Joseph Aoun & Naim Qassem". Starting relations with Lebanon are
  friendly instead of hostile.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Make armed-group areas their own states instead of highlighted overlays

Each group's area (host border ∩ control mask − pockets) is now cut
out of its host country at load time and added to the map as an
ordinary state, governed by the group's leader: e.g. Yemen (Houthis)
→ Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, Sudan (RSF) → Hemedti, Eastern Libya (LNA)
→ Khalifa Haftar, Abkhazia and South Ossetia as two states. Gaza
Strip (Hamas), Northern Cyprus and Somaliland already were states;
Sool and eastern Sanaag are moved from Somaliland to Somalia.

New states get economy/population (taken out of the host), a capital,
leaders, starting relations with host and patrons, and their aliases
now resolve to them in orders. The coloured overlays, labels and the
separate proxy click handler are gone, so they look and click like
every other country. A group is no longer listed as a non-state actor
inside the state it governs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Zoom buttons on the right edge; border-accurate control zones; Gaza, Cyprus fixes

- Zoom +/- now sit on the far right edge, in the gap between the
  Foreign Intelligence panel and the Diplomacy dock; they only step
  left of the panels when there is no room between them.
- Armed-group / breakaway zones are now the host country's real border
  intersected with a control mask for 1 January 2026, minus the pockets
  the group does not hold, so their outer edges match the country
  borders and coastlines exactly. Drawn with a solid border like the
  countries. Uses polygon-clipping (MIT), inlined.
- Palestine is split into two nations: West Bank (Mahmoud Abbas) and
  Gaza Strip (Hamas). Hamas's zone is Gaza west of the ceasefire
  "yellow line".
- Akrotiri and Dhekelia are now part of the United Kingdom, with RAF
  Akrotiri and the Dhekelia Garrison as British bases on the map.
- The UN buffer zone on Cyprus is no longer a selectable country.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Wumk2KgzeZLuaA1WiDsTrk

Add zoom in / zoom out buttons on the right side of the map

Adds a +/− button pair fixed to the right edge, vertically centred,
styled like the game's other buttons. They call map.zoomIn/zoomOut,
disable at min/max zoom, shift left to stay clear of the intel panel
and diplomacy dock, and remain visible in map-only mode.
